title: 电路的图：结点、支路、树与连支
statement: 电路如图（V_s1 = 10 V，I_s5 = 1 A，R_1 = 2 Ω，R_2 = R_3 = 4 Ω，R_4 = R_5 = 2 Ω，R_6 = 8 Ω）。画有向图时把 V_s1 与 R_1 的串联看成一条支路（支路 1），把 R_5 与 I_s5 的并联看成一条支路（支路 5），其余每个电阻一条支路；结点编号 1、2、3、4（4 接地），支路编号与方向见下方的有向图。
求图的结点数、支路数、树支数和连支数，判断哪一组支路是树，以及独立 KCL、KVL 方程的个数。

questions.explain: 结点 1、2、3、4。R_1 与 V_s1 之间的连接点不算图的结点：两者合成一条支路后，这个点只是支路内部的点。
8 个元件，但 V_s1–R_1 串联、R_5–I_s5 并联各合成一条支路，所以 b = 6。
树连通全部 n 个结点且不含回路，所以树支数 = n − 1 = 3，与选哪棵树无关。
l = b − n + 1 = 6 − 4 + 1 = 3：独立回路数（基本回路数）就是连支数，也是独立 KVL 方程数。

questions.ask: 下面哪一组支路构成一棵树？
choiceExplain: 2、3、6 首尾相接构成回路 1→2→3→1，结点 4 也没被连上。
4 条支路比 n − 1 = 3 多，一定含回路（这里是 1、6、5 构成的回路 4→1→3→4）。
只有两条支路，结点 1 没有连上。
questions.explain: 树：连通、包含全部结点、不含回路——支路数一定是 n − 1。

questions.ask: 对这个电路，独立的 KCL 方程和独立的 KVL 方程各有几个？
choiceExplain: 两处都多算了：KCL 少一个，KVL 只有连支数那么多。
对：n − 1 = 3 个 KCL（树支数），b − n + 1 = 3 个 KVL（连支数），合起来正好 b = 6 个，够解 6 个支路电流。
4 个结点的 KCL 方程相加恒为零，只有 3 个独立。
7 是图中所有回路的个数（三角形 4 个、四边形 3 个），并不独立。
questions.explain: n − 1 个独立 KCL、b − n + 1 个独立 KVL，总数 b。

hints: 只看拓扑：数结点时注意“标准支路”内部的点不算结点。
树：连通、无回路、包含全部结点；它的支路数与选哪棵树无关。
用 b − n + 1 算连支数，并逐个检查选项里有没有闭合回路。
solution: **数结点与支路。** 把 V_s1–R_1 串联、R_5–I_s5 并联各看成一条支路：结点 1、2、3、4，**n = 4**；支路 1～6，**b = 6**。
**连支。** l = b − n + 1 = **3**：每条连支加回树上都形成一个基本回路。
**独立方程。** KCL n − 1 = 3 个，KVL l = 3 个，共 6 = b 个——正好够求 6 个支路电流。

en.title: Graph of a circuit: nodes, branches, trees and links
statement: The circuit is drawn below (V_s1 = 10 V, I_s5 = 1 A, R_1 = 2 Ω, R_2 = R_3 = 4 Ω, R_4 = R_5 = 2 Ω, R_6 = 8 Ω). In the graph, V_s1 in series with R_1 counts as one branch (branch 1), R_5 in parallel with I_s5 as one branch (branch 5), and each other resistor as one branch; the nodes are numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 (4 is grounded) and the branch numbers and directions are those of the directed graph under the circuit.
Find the numbers of nodes, branches, tree branches and links, say which set of branches is a tree, and how many independent KCL and KVL equations there are.

questions.explain: Nodes 1, 2, 3, 4. The point between R_1 and V_s1 is not a node of the graph: once they form one branch, it is inside the branch.
8 elements, but V_s1–R_1 in series and R_5–I_s5 in parallel each form one branch, so b = 6.

questions.ask: Number of tree branches of any tree = ?
questions.explain: A tree connects all n nodes without a loop, so it has n − 1 = 3 branches whatever tree is chosen.
l = b − n + 1 = 6 − 4 + 1 = 3: the number of independent loops (fundamental loops) equals the number of links, and so does the number of independent KVL equations.

questions.ask: Which set of branches is a tree?
choiceExplain: Right. 1 (4–1), 2 (1–2) and 3 (2–3) connect all 4 nodes with 3 branches and no loop.
2, 3 and 6 close the loop 1→2→3→1, and node 4 is left out.
Four branches are more than n − 1 = 3, so there must be a loop (here 1, 6, 5: 4→1→3→4).
Only two branches: node 1 is not connected.
questions.explain: A tree is connected, contains every node and has no loop — so it always has n − 1 branches.

questions.ask: How many independent KCL and KVL equations does this circuit have?
choiceExplain: Both counts are too large: one KCL equation is dependent, and there are only as many KVL equations as links.
Right: n − 1 = 3 KCL equations (the tree branches) and b − n + 1 = 3 KVL equations (the links), b = 6 in total, enough for the 6 branch currents.
The 4 node equations add up to 0 = 0; only 3 are independent.
7 is the number of all loops of K4 (4 triangles and 3 quadrilaterals); they are not independent.
questions.explain: n − 1 independent KCL and b − n + 1 independent KVL equations, b in total.

hints: Topology only: points inside a standard branch are not nodes.
A tree is connected, loop-free and contains every node; its size does not depend on which tree you pick.
Use b − n + 1 for the links, and check each option for a closed loop.
solution: **Count.** Treat V_s1–R_1 in series and R_5–I_s5 in parallel as one branch each: nodes 1, 2, 3, 4, **n = 4**; branches 1–6, **b = 6**.

**Tree.** A tree connects every node without a loop, so it has n − 1 = **3** branches. {1, 2, 3} is a tree (4 to 1 via branch 1, then on to 2 and 3); {2, 3, 6} contains a loop, {1, 4, 5, 6} has one branch too many, {4, 5} is not connected.
**Links.** l = b − n + 1 = **3**: each link put back on the tree closes one fundamental loop.
**Independent equations.** n − 1 = 3 KCL and l = 3 KVL equations, 6 = b in total — exactly enough for the 6 branch currents.
